title: improv·artist · chromatic (Gerhard Richter)
mutation_directive: improv artist: chromatic via Gerhard Richter

improv_extras.practice: color-grid charts, squeegee abstracts; randomness as method

v1.feedback: The Richter color-chart grid is immediately legible and the squeegee smear animation is a genuine translation of the linked idea — you can read 'Farbtafel + horizontal drag' within two seconds. Palette is faithful and restrained (12 Richter hues, warm-grey smear target). To push it further: the grid cells are currently uniform random — Richter's actual charts use systematic permutation logic that creates visible chromatic gradients across the surface; implementing even a simple Latin-square or stripe-permutation would make the structure feel less like confetti and more like his deliberate color logic. The squeegee drag is nicely layered but the vertical wobble is too subtle to notice — either amplify it or drop it, and consider adding slight paint-thickness variation (point size modulated by drag distance) so smeared regions look physically thicker.

v2.feedback: The Richter Farbtafel concept lands well — the Latin-square color grid is a smart translation of his color charts into particles, and the squeegee smear mechanic is a genuine formal idea, not a gimmick. The 12-hue palette is well-chosen and restrained enough to read as Richter rather than random. Two things to refine: the smear band could be wider and more aggressive — right now it's subtle enough that a first-time viewer might miss the squeegee pass entirely, which undercuts the whole concept. Consider adding a slight impasto effect (particle size variation within cells) even in the un-smeared state, so the grid reads more as thick paint and less as a flat pixel grid.
